subject: P06
required_fixes: P06-F1 (high): Preserve a completed turn when shutdown interrupts its pending history export. This is the C19 lifecycle/C20 persistence boundary, also affecting C21/C22 call evidence. In crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:1894-1941, end_turn clears turn and latest, settles every Streaming entry, publishes Ready/lastTurn, then requests HistoryRead. Until that response arrives, a fully displayed completed turn is unsaved. Sleep, End or Quit makes drive return immediately through its cancellation branch (:956-959); stop-time persistence at :569-574 then sees neither turn_open nor a Streaming entry and skips saving. No save failure is set on this cancellation path. On the first turn the entire conversation disappears after relaunch; after a prior save, history silently omits the latest completed answer and any completed tool result/trace, while savedAt may still describe the older record. C22's open-turn fix remains valid but cannot cover this post-turn export window. Track unsaved transcript state through export settlement, or complete the bounded export before stopping; when no matching export can be obtained, preserve inspect-only protected work rather than fabricate replay or reuse a mismatched older export. Acceptance: hold HistoryRead after turn/completed, stop via the lifecycle path before export timeout, relaunch offline and read the latest messages and actual tool outcomes. Cover a first turn and an updated existing record; no continuation without a valid matching replay and no automatic remote replay on reconnect.
evidence_gaps: P06-G1: Add integrated stop-during-export coverage for P06-F1. refused_or_unanswered_exports_and_refused_restores_are_named at crates/desktop-core/tests/harness_identity_history/main.rs:638 waits for an explicit refusal or the full timeout; it does not stop while the completed turn's export is pending. The C22 persistence tests stop while a turn is still open. The current 38 native checks and passing suites therefore do not establish retention across this remaining lifecycle/persistence window.
